transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… my body’s been feeling kind of out of my control. I was pacing around my apartment all night, making notes for this supper-club idea, and now lately I’m so slowed down my sister says it takes me forever just to put my shoes on.
Have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people don’t?
I don’t think so. Not like… voices or seeing people that aren’t there. I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Have you had times when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or on top of the world?

Yeah… I guess so. After I got fired, I felt… weirdly unstoppable. Like excited, like I could do anything. But if someone questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d get really angry. Like they were trying to wreck everything.
During that period when you felt unstoppable, did you have beliefs that other people said were not true or didn’t make sense?

Yeah… I mean, I was sure I was about to start the best bilingual supper club in the city. I thought investors would be idiots not to give me money, even though… I didn’t have a job or anything lined up.
Are you feeling depressed most of the day lately?
I don’t know… not really sure how to answer that. I’ve been down sometimes, but most of the day? I haven’t really been keeping track.
Have you ever had a delusion or heard voices during a time when your mood was otherwise normal?
I… I’m not really sure. I don’t think so? Not when I was feeling normal, at least. I’d have to think about it.
Lately, have you been feeling sad or empty most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not sure. I’ve felt low here and there, but I don’t know if I’d say most of the day nearly every day.
Since you started feeling slowed down, have you had any beliefs that other people said weren’t true or didn’t make sense?
I don’t think so. I mean… I’ve felt off, but I can’t really point to some belief like that.
Lately, have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
Yeah… kind of. Stuff I usually like—cooking, music, taking food pictures, soccer… even volunteering—it just feels flat. Like I remember caring about it, but I can’t really feel that right now.
Right now, do you feel sad or empty most of the day?
I don’t know… I feel off, kind of low sometimes, but I’m not sure I’d call it sad or empty most of the day.
Right now, do you feel hopeless?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of it that way… just feels hard to see much past right now.
Right now, have you been having thoughts that life isn’t worth living?
I… I don’t know. I don’t think about it that clearly. It’s more just… I’m tired of things feeling like this.
Are you having thoughts of killing yourself?
I… I don’t know. I don’t really want to answer that.
Right now, are you feeling depressed?
I don’t know… maybe. I just feel kind of shut down. Hard to put a word on it.
Right now, do you feel depressed?
I’m not really sure. It feels… heavy, I guess, but I don’t know if I’d call it depressed.
Right now, are you sleeping much more than usual?
I don’t know. I haven’t really been keeping track… I guess I sleep when I can.
Right now, do you feel like your body and movements are slowed down?
Yeah… lately, yeah. I feel really slowed down. Like even getting my shoes on takes forever—my sister noticed it. It’s like my body isn’t really doing what I want.
Right now, do you feel sad most of the day?
I… I don’t really know. Sad, maybe sometimes, but “most of the day” is hard to say.
Right now, are you feeling hopeless?
I’m… not sure. I don’t really want to get into that.
Right now, do you still enjoy anything?
Not really. Things I usually like—cooking, music, soccer, even taking food pictures—it all just feels kind of flat. Like I remember caring, but I don’t feel it right now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview clearly confirms a manic episode with elevated/expansive mood, irritability, marked increased activity/pacing, and grandiose beliefs about an unrealistic supper-club venture. However, psychotic symptoms were not established: the patient denied hallucinations, was unsure about delusions outside mood episodes, and the reported grandiose business belief does not clearly meet the threshold for definite psychosis in the interview. Current depressive features are present (anhedonia, psychomotor retardation, feeling low/shut down), but a full severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms was not established. Therefore the best fit among the provided options is bipolar affective disorder, current episode manic without psychotic symptoms.
